listen.explanationKey: What amendment says all persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are U.S. citizens?
facts: After the Civil War, the 14th Amendment said that all persons born or naturalized in the United States are citizens.
In 1870, the 15th Amendment said a man could not be kept from voting because of his race.
But for almost one hundred years after that, many Black Americans were still kept from voting by unfair rules and violence. The civil rights movement fought to change this.

newWords.meaning: a change or addition to the Constitution
a group of people, often by skin color or where their families come from
the rights every citizen should have
the amendment that says race cannot stop a citizen from voting

story.say: After the Civil War, new amendments were added to the Constitution.

help.simpler: After the war, the Constitution was changed three times.
help.why: Two of these amendments are on the test.

story.say: The 14th Amendment said that all persons born or naturalized in the United States are citizens.

help.simpler: If you are born here or naturalize here, you are a citizen.
help.example: Naturalize means to become a citizen after applying.
help.why: The test asks which amendment says this: the 14th.

check.prompt: Tap the amendment about who is a citizen.

story.say: In 1870, the 15th Amendment said a man could not be kept from voting because of his race.

help.simpler: In 1870, voting rules could not keep men out because of race.
help.example: Race means a group of people seen as having the same skin color or roots.
help.why: “1870” and “15th Amendment” are answers on the test.

story.say: So “1870”, “after the Civil War” and “the 15th Amendment” all answer: When did all men get the right to vote?

help.simpler: Three answers, one question: 1870, after the Civil War, the 15th Amendment.
help.example: You only need to say one of them.
help.why: The test asks when all men got the right to vote.

check.prompt: When did all men get the right to vote?

story.say: But for almost one hundred years after that, many Black Americans were still kept from voting.

help.simpler: The law changed, but many Black Americans still could not vote.
help.why: It shows that a law on paper is not always followed.

story.say: They were kept from voting by unfair rules and violence.

help.simpler: Unfair rules and attacks stopped people from voting.
help.example: Some places made Black Americans pass hard tests or pay to vote.
help.why: It explains why the fight for voting rights went on.

story.say: The civil rights movement fought to change this.

help.simpler: Many people worked together for equal rights.
help.example: Martin Luther King, Jr. was a leader of the civil rights movement.
help.why: You will learn more about civil rights in Unit 6.

check.statement: After 1870, every Black American could vote freely.

readIt.sentence: Who has the right to vote?

writeIt.sentence: Citizens have the right to vote.

listen.explanationKey: Name one leader of the women’s rights movement in the 1800s.
facts: In the 1800s, women could not vote in most of the country.
Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton led the fight for women's right to vote.

Sojourner Truth and Harriet Tubman were born into slavery and escaped. They spoke out for the rights of women and of Black Americans. Harriet Tubman also helped many enslaved people escape to freedom.
In 1920, after World War I, the 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote.

newWords.meaning: a group of people working together for a change
the amendment that gave women the right to vote

story.say: In the 1800s, women could not vote in most of the country.

help.simpler: Back then, most women were not allowed to vote.
help.example: Only men could vote in most states.
help.why: This is why the women’s rights movement began.

story.say: Susan B. Anthony led the fight for women’s right to vote.

help.simpler: Anthony worked her whole life so women could vote.
help.example: She gave speeches and wrote about women’s rights.
help.why: “Susan B. Anthony” is an answer on the test.

story.say: Elizabeth Cady Stanton led the fight too.

help.simpler: Stanton was another leader for women’s rights.
help.example: She and Anthony worked together for many years.
help.why: “Elizabeth Cady Stanton” is an answer on the test.

check.prompt: Name one leader of the women’s rights movement in the 1800s.

story.say: Sojourner Truth was born into slavery and escaped.

help.simpler: Sojourner Truth was enslaved, then got away to freedom.
help.why: “Sojourner Truth” is an answer on the test.

story.say: She spoke out for the rights of women and of Black Americans.

help.simpler: She gave speeches for equal rights for women and Black Americans.
help.example: To speak out means to say in public what you believe.
help.why: It explains why she is a leader of the movement.

check.statement: Sojourner Truth spoke out for the rights of women.

story.say: Harriet Tubman was also born into slavery and escaped.

help.simpler: Harriet Tubman was enslaved, then got away to freedom.
help.why: “Harriet Tubman” is an answer on the test.

story.say: She spoke out for women and Black Americans, and helped many enslaved people escape to freedom.

help.simpler: Tubman went back many times to lead others to freedom.
help.example: She helped many enslaved people escape to the North.
help.why: It explains why Tubman is so well known.

story.say: In 1920, after World War I, the 19th Amendment gave women the right to vote.

help.example: The 19th Amendment changed the Constitution so women could vote.
help.why: “1920”, “after World War I” and “19th Amendment” are answers.

check.prompt: Tap the amendment that gave women the right to vote.
When did all women get the right to vote?
